TA0014.title: Money Laundering Gangs
TA0014.description:
Money laundering gangs are teams in the fraud, gambling, and cybercrime chains responsible for cleaning and transferring illicit funds. After receiving upstream proceeds, they wash funds white and return them via multi-tier account splitting, score-running laundering platforms (AT0039), virtual-currency exchange (AT0040), and four-party payment (AT0026). Their operations typically divide labor into ATM cash-out runners (TA0014-001), card farmers (providing bank-card sets), and score-running collectors (collecting and paying via personal QR codes).

They use personal codes, merchant codes (T0317-002), and aggregated payment channels to split funds in high-frequency small amounts, then sever the money trail via virtual-currency mixing, cross-border exchange, and sham trade to evade AML monitoring and police investigation. Their laundering directly drives virtual-currency money laundering (R0060), score-running laundering (R0093), and payment-channel abuse (R0094), and is the cash-out key of telecom-fraud and cross-border gambling chains, routinely collaborating with black-market organizations (TA0017) and fraud gangs (TA0015).

references.title: How Much Do You Know About 'Money Laundering Rooms'?

TA0014-001.title: ATM Runner
TA0014-001.description: A person who withdraws fraud proceeds from ATMs in exchange for a commission. They are commonly called 'runners' because they typically travel by motorcycle or electric scooter to carry out the withdrawals.

references.title: A Batch of 'ATM Runners' Arrested with 2.7 Million Cash Seized — Why Have They Resurfaced After Years of Silence?
